description: An alias REPLACES the table name: with FROM sr AS x, a reference qualified by the ORIGINAL name is "SQL compilation error: invalid identifier 'SR.C'" - measured in the SELECT list, WHERE, GROUP BY and ORDER BY alike. The alias itself, the unaliased original name, and derived-table aliases all keep resolving. The SELECT-list rejection is PLAN-time and fires over an EMPTY table, like live's compile-time error; the WHERE / GROUP BY / ORDER BY forms still need rows to flow through key resolution - an ORDER BY over one row short-circuits before resolving - so the fixture uses two rows. Converted 1:1 from query/AliasShadowingTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sr (t INTEGER, c INTEGER)
SELECT sr.t FROM sr AS x
SELECT x.t FROM sr AS x WHERE sr.c = 2
SELECT x.t FROM sr AS x GROUP BY sr.t, x.t
SELECT x.t FROM sr AS x ORDER BY sr.c
CREATE TABLE sr (t INTEGER, c INTEGER)
SELECT sr.t FROM sr AS x
CREATE TABLE sr (t INTEGER, c INTEGER)
SELECT x.t FROM sr AS x WHERE x.c = 2
SELECT sr.t FROM sr WHERE sr.c = 2
SELECT x.t FROM sr AS x GROUP BY x.t ORDER BY x.t
SELECT sub.t FROM (SELECT t FROM sr) AS sub ORDER BY sub.t
